correctness.rationale: For finite graphs with positive edge weights and gamma>0, R(f)=max(f,0) is linear on each sign orthant, giving global two-point Lipschitz modulus max_S ||D_S||_A (attained locally). For A=I+gamma L, cut blocks X,Y,B, a Schur complement gives ||D_S||_A=(1-rho(S)^2)^(-1/2) with rho=||X^-1/2 B Y^-1/2||<1. Edgewise Cauchy–Schwarz plus crossing degrees c_i<=Delta yields rho<=gamma Delta/(1+gamma Delta), hence Lip<=(1+gamma Delta)/sqrt(1+2gamma Delta). Equality propagates positive maximizers to a whole bipartite component with weighted degree Delta, and any such component supplies equal singular vectors. Unit star Schur elimination gives exact sqrt(1+n gamma^2/[1+(n+1)gamma]); one-point energy contraction and nontrivial two-point expansion are compatible. Edgeless, isolated/disconnected boundary cases accounted for.

evidence: One-point Dirichlet contraction and spectral Kantorovich inequalities are broader in some directions but not a complete graph rigidity characterization.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A bound on ||R(f)|| versus ||f|| for a single f cannot control ||R(f)-R(g)|| by a trivial substitution because R is nonlinear; spectral estimates do not characterize bipartite weighted-regular saturation without extra graph analysis.

evidence: An edge always gives rho(S)>0 and hence Lip(R)>1 in the augmented Sobolev norm.
